figures.finding: A minor's legal act needs the consent of the minor's representative (the parents as guardians), given in advance or after, for one act or a kind of acts; without it the representative may set the act aside within a month of learning of it, unless minors of that age usually do such acts and it does the minor no real harm; an act that would need a court's approval if the representative did it needs that approval. A minor living with the parents uses income from work, in fair measure, for the family household and the minor's own needs; no share is set aside. The rule covers any legal act, so a writing, directing or performing contract alike.

value.binding: representative's consent (s. 4); court approval where s. 7 requires it
value.earnings: used in fair measure for the household and the minor's needs (s. 23(a))

figures.finding: No child under 15 may be employed; a child of 15 still under compulsory schooling works only as an apprentice or with the Education Ministry's exemption or certificate; the Minister of Labour may permit work from 14 for a child exempt from compulsory schooling, and a child of 14 may do light work in the official school holidays as the Minister's regulations allow. The Law calls a person under 16 a child and one of 16 to 18 a young person.

figures.finding: A child under 15 may not be employed in a public, artistic or advertising performance or in filming for advertising, rehearsals and training included, unless the Minister of Labour and Welfare permits it for a limited period for that particular child, and never in the child's school hours; from 15 to 18 a young person may be engaged or brokered for advertising (modelling included) only with the young person's and a parent's consent on the prescribed form, which the employer keeps seven years, and a parent or adult relative may be present. Hours by age are in the 1999 performance regulations, not read. The rule names performance only; a young writer or director falls under the general working age (15).

(ב) על אף הוראות סעיף קטן (א) וסעיף 2, רשאי שר העבודה והרווחה לתת היתר, לתקופה מוגבלת, להעסקתו של ילד פלוני או לתיווך להעסקתו של אותו ילד, בהופעה או בצילומים כאמור בסעיף קטן (א), ובלבד שלא יינתן היתר להעסקה כאמור בשעות הלימודים של הילד. ... (ד) מעסיק של נער בהופעת פרסום ישמור את הסכמת הנער וההורה שניתנה לפי סעיף קטן (ב) או (ג) שבע שנים מתום תקופת העסקת הנער אצלו.

figures.finding: The Israel Film Fund's main production scheme sets no age: the screenwriter has no threshold, the producer must be active, with a produced and screened or broadcast feature behind them, and own a registered production company (or be a licensed dealer who forms a partnership for the film), and the director must have directed a 60-minute feature or 50 minutes of drama in aggregate for a recognised body; a producer whose experience is a spouse's or relative's film needs the Fund's approval.

value.producer: proven feature experience; owns a registered production company or licensed dealer in partnership
value.director: 60-min feature or 50 min of drama aggregate

figures.applies: IFF English guidelines (2024 file, 'for information purposes only'); the Hebrew regulations were not read. The company or dealer requirement brings the producer under company and capacity law (majority 18).

sources.said: Screenwriter - There is no threshold requirement. Producer - The producer must be an active producer with proven professional experience in the production of a 60-minute-long or 150-minute-long feature drama film which was produced and screened and/or broadcast and who owns a registered production company (or who is a licensed dealer who will maintain a partnership for the needs of the film, if approved).
